headline: California law requires companies to connect customers to a person within 15 minutes
body: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 1609, the Right to Human Customer Service Act, on Sept. 28. The law takes effect Jan. 1, 2027 and requires companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue to connect a customer with a person within 15 minutes of the request, or to book a call-back within one business day.
note: For companies running AI service bots, the law turns the handoff into a fixed clock, and only public prosecutors can enforce it.

evidence.text: California’s AB 1609 takes effect Jan. 1, 2027, and gives businesses with more than $500 million in revenue 15 minutes to connect a customer with a person or book a call back, with fines of up to $5,000 per violation.
Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 1609, the Right to Human Customer Service Act , on Sept. 28.

The law requires companies with more than $500 million in annual revenue to connect a customer with a person within 15 minutes of the request, or to book a specific call-back time within one business day.
Only public prosecutors can enforce the law, with fines of up to $5,000 for a first violation and $10,000 for each one after.

The California Chamber of Commerce opposed the bill, arguing that a fixed clock would push agents to end calls faster to reach the next person in the queue, and that handling account issues by phone raises security risks .
